item.text:
**4B.10 Research Note**
Overall read: **weaker than inherited, though the formal transfer still happened cleanly**. Jokowi ended 2024 with a constitutional handover intact, but the evidence points to lower democratic resilience than the baseline he inherited: more patronage/dynastic politics, more politicized institutions, weaker media freedom, and more digital/administrative pressure on dissent.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Analysis-A decade of Jokowi: Indonesia’s democracy icon leaves illiberal legacy, critics say | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-10-14 | <https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/> | Reuters’ end-of-term analysis says Jokowi left behind strong growth and infrastructure, but also patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity than when he entered office. This is the clearest high-level judgment that political freedom and democratic resilience ended **weaker** than inherited. | `4B.10`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.8` |
| Indonesia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | <https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-world/2024> | Freedom House rated Indonesia “Partly Free” and said it had made major democratic gains since 1998, but still faced systemic corruption, discrimination, Papua conflict, and politicized defamation/blasphemy laws. It also flagged the 2023 court ruling that enabled Gibran’s candidacy as a serious institutional warning sign. This supports a finding that Jokowi left the system **less resilient** than a clean inheritance would imply. | `4B.10`, `4B.7`, `4B.8` |
| Indonesia: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | <https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-net/2024> | The report says Kominfo could directly restrict content without appeals, election-period monitoring targeted “hoax” content, and critics/journalists/internet users faced prosecution, harassment, and self-censorship. That is strong evidence that democratic resilience in the information sphere weakened under Jokowi rather than strengthening. | `4B.10`, `4B.6`, `4B.9` |
| 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Indonesia | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12; covers 2024 | <https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html> | The report says there were no significant human-rights changes in 2024 and documents serious restrictions on freedom of expression and media freedom, plus weak accountability for abuses. That is negative evidence for any claim that Jokowi left political freedom stronger than he found it. | `4B.10`, `4B.4`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`, `4B.9` |
| Farewell-Welcome Ceremony for Indonesia’s President from Jokowi to Prabowo Subianto | Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | 2024-10-20 | <https://setkab.go.id/en/farewell-welcome-ceremony-for-indonesias-president-from-jokowi-to-prabowo-subianto/> | Jokowi formally transferred power to Prabowo on inauguration day. This is the strongest positive evidence in the set: the constitutional handover occurred on schedule, so the **formal succession rule** survived even if the broader democratic environment worsened. | `4B.10`, `4B.8` |
| Indonesia court rejects election disputes, upholding president-elect Prabowo’s win | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-04-22 | <https://theprint.in/world/indonesia-court-rejects-election-disputes-upholding-president-elect-prabowos-win/2051390/> | The Constitutional Court said there was no evidence of systematic fraud or presidential meddling and that state bodies had not been mobilized to sway the vote. This is a limited positive signal that formal institutions still constrained the ruler, but it does not outweigh the broader evidence of democratic backsliding. | `4B.10`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.8` |
| Indonesia’s president-elect Prabowo secures parliamentary majority | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-08-16 | <https://theprint.in/world/indonesias-president-elect-prabowo-secures-parliamentary-majority/2225570/> | Reuters reported that NasDem joined Prabowo’s coalition, smoothing the transition into the next government. This is a modest positive signal for post-election governability, but it is more about elite accommodation than a net gain in democratic resilience. | `4B.10`, `4B.8` |

**Bottom line**
- **Positive:** the 2024 constitutional transfer happened, the court process stood, and the next government formed without a rupture.
- **Negative:** the broader system ended with more patronage, dynastic politics, politicized institutions, digital controls, and media pressure than the democratic baseline Jokowi inherited.

**Search gap**
- I did not find credible evidence that Jokowi left Indonesia’s political freedom **stronger** in a broad sense.
- The main positive evidence is limited to formal succession and some institutional continuity, not an overall improvement in democratic resilience.
